paragraphs: The Defender P525 is part of the modern L663 generation, introduced in 2021 for the 90 and later offered in the US-market 110 from 2026. It uses the AJ133 — a 5.0-litre supercharged V8 that Land Rover has applied across several performance-oriented models, including the Range Rover Sport SVR and Velar SVAutobiography. The P525 badge denotes a specific power tune of this engine, rather than a mechanically unique unit. No Defender-specific known issue is confirmed for this application — it's generally considered a reliable engine in this chassis, though like any performance V8, regular maintenance is still critical.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace AJ133 engines for every Defender P525 on the road.

cards.body: A 5.0-litre supercharged V8 fitted to the Defender P525 from 2021 (90) and 2026 (US-market 110). The P525 badge reflects the power output tune of this engine. While the AJ133 is generally reliable and shares the broader supercharged V8 pattern used across other Land Rover models, no Defender-specific issue is confirmed for this application. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every P525 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the P525 is one of several power-tune badges on the same AJ133 engine, it's important to confirm the exact tune and specification when sourcing any replacement parts or a full replacement unit. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (AJ133) via registration or VIN - Your body style (90 or 110) - Year of manufacture - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build
